fortuneWheel.summary: A polished Persian RTL prize-wheel experience backed by strict server-side award integrity. The browser animates a result chosen and persisted by Django; it never selects or submits the prize itself.
fortuneWheel.video_hint: This space is ready for the YouTube walkthrough.
fortuneWheel.overview: Build a responsive prize wheel where administrators preassign coupons, users receive exactly the intended award, and retries or interrupted requests cannot consume extra coupons. The interface is fully localized in Persian and designed for right-to-left reading.
fortuneWheel.architecture: Coupon selection, redemption, and spin creation run inside one PostgreSQL transaction with row locking. Every spin uses a client-generated idempotency key, so replaying a request returns the original immutable award. Pending attempts survive reloads and remain isolated across browser tabs.
fortuneWheel.quality: The project ships as a three-service Docker Compose stack with Django and Gunicorn, PostgreSQL, and an Nginx-served React build. Backend tests cover concurrency, rollback, ownership, authentication, CSRF, catalog rules, and audit immutability; frontend tests cover 288 rotation cases, protocol errors, recovery, accessibility, and dialog behavior.
highlights: Server-authoritative prizes with immutable historical snapshots
Exactly-once behavior through idempotency and transactional locking
Reload and multi-tab recovery without duplicate coupon consumption
Accessible, responsive Persian RTL interface with a twelve-sector wheel

alpr.disclosure: This is an employer-owned, team-developed proprietary project. This page describes only my selected engineering contributions and intentionally excludes source code, customer data, production screens, internal performance figures, and proprietary implementation details.
alpr.overview: I contributed to selected parts of a team-developed Automatic License Plate Recognition platform used for real-time vehicle-monitoring workflows. My work involved full-stack integration across Python services, computer-vision processing, APIs, and a web dashboard.
alpr.challenges: Contributed to backend image-processing workflows, API boundaries, real-time event delivery, and dashboard integration. The work required coordinating asynchronous processing with a responsive operator interface while keeping the system maintainable across service boundaries.
alpr.result: This experience strengthened my ability to connect computer-vision workloads with production web systems, reason about real-time data flow, and collaborate on a multi-service product without exposing confidential implementation details.
